question.problem: Find the point of the intersection of the elliptic cone $2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$ and the line $x=y=\frac{z+8}{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of our line in parametric form:

$$
x=y=\frac{z+8}{2}=t\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}x=t \\ y=t \\ z=2t-8,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Substituting the above expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ 2{t}^{2}+2{t}^{2} & =(2t-8)^{2} \\ 4{t}^{2} & =4{t}^{2}-32t+64 \\ 32t & =64 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute our solution back into the equations of the line. For $t=2,$ we have

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=2 \\ y=2 \\ z=2(2)-8=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(2,2,-4).$
